newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity U.S. stock funds flow flat in December.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity U.S. stock funds flow flat in December.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said it estimated cash flows into its domestic equity funds will turn flat after more than a $1 billion inflow in November.
Investors sold the domestic stock funds during the first couple of weeks of December when the stock markets turned volatile following November's strong gains, said Robyn Tice, a Fidelity spokeswoman.

They moved back into the funds once the markets calmed later in December, she said. In addition, for tax purchases, investors generally put off purchasing equity funds until after the funds paid dividends, Tice said.
The most popular domestic stock funds during December were Fidelity Real Estate Fund, Fidelity Low-Priced Stock Fund and Fidelity Select Electronics Fund, she said.

Cash flows into other sectors in December reflected November's flows, she said. Flows from international equity funds were expected to be "slightly negative" again, bonds were "slightly positive" and investors poured more than $1 billion into money market funds for the second month in a row, Tice said.

"We expect the money markets to pull in more than a billion in net sales this month. A lot of the response is to the record highs and (investors) looking for a place to put the money until the market's volatility rides out," she said.
